content:
Anya: Thinking we should consolidate the console permission checks into a small permission-surface service rather than scattering pushdown logic across every query path. Thoughts?

Samir: Curious — what's the main win here vs keeping checks in the query layer?

Anya: Twofold: 1) single place to reason about semantics (canRead, canEdit, row-level filters) and 2) consistent cache keys so we can cache decision results across UI routes.

Miguel: Concern: extra network hop on every panel render. p99 latency budget for panels is tight. How do we avoid adding ~5-10ms per request? :thinking:

Anya: Plan is to make the surface synchronous for small checks (boolean allow lists) and async-prefetch for heavier filter materialization. For heavy ones we attach a cache token to the query.

Jess: Example interface?

Anya: Draft API sketch:
```http
POST /v1/permissions/evaluate
Body: {"user_id":"u-123","view_id":"view-stats","resource_hint":"panel-rows","context":{"tenant_id":"t-9"}}
Response: {"allowed":true,"cache_key":"perm:u-123:v-view-stats:t-9:v1","filters":[{"field":"tenant_id","op":"=","value":"t-9"}] }
```

Miguel: Ok the cache_key idea is good — we can include that into existing query cache keys so we don't re-evaluate. Need TTL guidance though.

Samir: Tradeoffs: if we cache too long and an admin changes role, users will have stale perms. Invalidation complexity is a real ops burden.

Anya: Agreed. Suggested approach: short absolute TTL (30s) + event-driven invalidation for role/assignment changes. Invalidate by prefixing with role-version.

Jess: For pushdown vs post-filtering: pushing filters into the storage layer reduces bandwidth but complicates query planning for our tiling service. If we always push a filter we might fragment tile cache.

Miguel: Good point — we should avoid making tile keys explode. Maybe only push down a small canonical tenant filter; any non-trivial dynamic predicates we apply client-side as fallback.

Samir: So proposal: permission-surface returns (1) allow boolean, (2) canonical pushdown filters (only a tiny set: tenant, org_id, partition) and (3) an optional client-side safe-filter that is applied after query. That limits cache explosion.

Anya: Exactly. Also we'll add a "hint" flag to indicate whether the filter is stable (safe to bake into tile key) or ephemeral.

infra-bot: deploy.provision: staging-perm-surface v0.1 deployed to staging (job 4821) :rocket:

Jess: Rollout plan? feature flag, gated by views that opt-in?

Anya: Start with onboarding dashboards that are low QPS. Backfill a small set of panels that can tolerate a 20ms cold miss. Metric guardrails: incrementally roll when 95th percentile panel latency delta < +8ms and no increase in error rates.

Miguel: Observability checklist: per-request perm evaluation time, cache hit rate, invalidation event latency, and tile cache fragmentation metrics. We should expose these on the console health dashboard.

Samir: One more: how do we sign/verify cache_key so it can't be forged client-side?

Anya: Server signs cache_key with HMAC and the query-side verifies signature before using it. That keeps the query layer from trusting user-provided keys.

Jess: Backwards compatibility: old dashboards should keep current behavior until they opt in. Also provide an opt-out flag on the tile service for early rollback.

Miguel: Performance experiment idea: A/B route half of panel requests through perm-surface and half through current inline checks. Measure cost per request and user-visible latency.

Samir: For ACL storage: normalized roles + precomputed view grants. We should avoid scanning large role grants per eval — use denormalized grants keyed by (view_id, role_id).

Anya: Implementation notes: lightweight gRPC endpoint, rate-limited, horizontally scalable, with a local LRU for hot keys. We'll keep the decision logic as pure functions for easy testing.

Jess: Security: log decisions but avoid PII in logs. Tie audit events to admin changes for compliance.

Miguel: Ops: prepare a rollback playbook: 1) flip feature flag off, 2) fast invalidate perm-surface local caches, 3) monitor error budget.

Anya: Next steps: I'll open a short RFC outlining API shape + invalidation semantics. Miguel/Samir/Jess — can you +1 on the rollout/invalidation approach or add objections?

Samir: +1 on approach, will add a note about role-change propagation latency.

Miguel: +1, want to see the tile-key heuristics in the RFC before we push to more panels.

Jess: +1, please include observability dashboards and the canary test plan in the RFC.

infra-bot: reminder: staging-perm-surface metrics collection started (job 4821) :eyes:
